Hybrid technique for optimal location and cost
sizing of thyristor controlled series
compensator to upgrade voltage stability
ISSN 1751-8687
Received on 7th October 2015
Revised on 26th December 2015
Accepted on 27th January 2016
doi: 10.1049/iet-gtd.2015.1211

Sheila Mahapatra 1 ✉, A.N. Jha 2, B.K. Panigrahi 2
1School of Engineering and Technology, The Northcap University, Haryana, India
2Department of Electrical Engineering, IIT, Delhi, India
✉ E-mail: mahapatrasheila@gmail.com
Abstract: In this study, a hybrid technique is employed for ameliorating the voltage stability of test system with thyristor
controlled series compensator (TCSC) installation. Improved gravitational search algorithm is used to first set the optimal
location of TCSC to generate optimal power flow solution under normal and contingency condition while firefly algorithm
is utilised to improve voltage stability and TCSC cost sizing , respectively. The proposed te chnique is implemented in
MATLAB working platform and the power flow security and v oltage stability is evaluated with IEEE 6, 14 and 30 bus
transmission systems. The optimal TCSC placement is governed by new proposed index of apparent power flow index.
The performance of the proposed method is deduced to be superior when results are compared with traditional
gravitational search algorithm (GSA) and other hybrid methods of fuzzy-GSA and radial bas is function neural network
techniques.
1 Introduction
Planning and real time operation of power system is largely
dependent on optimal power ﬂow (OPF) and the emergence of
competitive power market generates the obligation of minimising
generation cost and system losses integrated with voltage stability.
The OPF practically coordinates the power ﬂow with gainful
dispatch thus preparing for reduction in expense capacities by
taking into record equality and inequality parameters [
1, 2]. The
problem of voltage instability is aggravated in application of open
market principles where systems are generally operated close to
their stability margins to attain maximum operational cost
reduction. The traditional approach of Newton ’s strategy and direct
programming are confronted with issues of being trapped in local
minima, embraces losses and may not be adequately utilised to
generate optimal solution [
3–5]. Exceptional among the ﬂexible
AC transmission systems (FACTS) devices, thyristor controlled
series compensator (TCSC) is invested with unfathomable
application potential in unequivocally controlling the power ﬂow
on transmission line, damping power oscillations and venturing up
transient robustness [
6]. Numerous stochastic techniques like
Genetic Algorithms (GA), Evolutionary Programming (EP) and
Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO), have been adequately utilised
to effectively address the OPF problem with and without using
FACTS controllers [
7–9]. Nireekshana et al. [10] were
instrumental in determination and change of available transfer
capability in the deregulated working of power systems by static
Var compensator and TCSC. Generally, most work stated in
literature consider OPF and voltage stability issues independently
but in open electricity markets it is imperative to consider voltage
stability limits while accounting for pro ﬁtable dispatch for overall
system security.
The work delivered in this paper proposes a novel hybrid technique
for optimising the location and cost sizing of TCSC resulting in
secured OPF with retention of voltage consistency of the
transmission system to prevent voltage collapse under variable load
conditions. Two vital issues are considered: ﬁrst is optimal TCSC
placement for impregnable and reliable OPF solution under normal
and contingency condition and second is to include voltage stability
criteria in the original OPF objective function and TCSC cost
reduction. The OPF problem is thus reformulated to elevate
emphasis on voltage stability. The remnant of the paper is presented
as follows: Section 2 offers problem formulation followed by a
detailed view of the proposed methods implemented. The results on
three standard IEEE benchmark systems endorse the superiority of
t h ep r o p o s e dm e t h o d .
2 Problem formulation
The TCSC is home to a sequence of compensating capacitors shunted
by the thyristor controlled reactor. In this model, the controllable
reactance is integrated in series to transmission line and the line
impedance is adapted. As a result, the apparent power going
through the line is either perked up to maximum or scaled down to
minimum depending on loading conditions. The two objectives
considered are secured OPF with optimal TCSC placement under
normal and overloading state and evaluation of TCSC capacity in
accordance with voltage variation and cost function.

3 Computational techniques implementation
In this section, the intelligent and hybrid methods implemented to
obtain optimal location and cost sizing of TCSC for OPF coupled
with voltage stability are presented. The optimal location and
injected capacity of TCSC depend on the security indices of
apparent power ﬂow and cost function. The evaluation of
effectiveness of each algorithm is analysed in two phases: ﬁrst
phase establishes optimal location of TCSC resulting in enhanced
OPF and the second involves TCSC cost sizing and improving
voltage pro ﬁle. Subsequently, the injection capacity of TCSC is
calculated by (8) and (9) through the security constraints. The
IEEE standard bench mark 6, 14 and 30 bus systems are used for
analysis and initially normal power ﬂow and the stability
conditions are determined and later the loading faults are
introduced in the bus system. The detailed explanation of these
computational methods is provided below.
3.1 Gravitational search algorithm
The gravitational search algorithm (GSA) has astonishingly arrived
as one of the rewarding stochastic search techniques rooted on
Newtonian laws of gravity and mass interaction [
13]. In GSA,
efﬁciency of the agents is evaluated by their masses which are
deemed as objectives. The gravitational forces of attraction
between the objects trigger a complete motion towards the objects
which possesses heavier masses that procure superior ﬁtness
values and the best solution is approached as against the lesser
ones which signify the worst solution. Each and every mass has
the position in the order such as inertial mass, active gravitational
mass and passive gravitational mass. The mass position amounts
to the solution of objective function and the ﬁtness function
employed is indicated by the gravitational and the initial masses
[
14]. Traditional GSA method has low convergence due to
increased randomness associated with agent ’s velocity which is
suitably curbed by various hybrid techniques being integrated with
it. Hybrid methods based on traditional GSA algorithm which are
implemented in the problem to enhance the system performance
are as follows.

to uncertainties. Sequentially, to manage these unpredictability in
solutions and to keep away detonation and deviation, velocity
constraint is introduced which is predicted by fuzzy logic. The
inputs of fuzzy system are current velocity of agents vd

4 Results and discussion
In this paper, innovative hybrid techniques based on GSA is executed
in MATLAB platform and their performances are evaluated on IEEE
standard bench mark system of 6 and 14 buses, respectively. Among
all the methods implemented in the test systems, IGSA-FA
computational technique provides superior results. TCSC installation
elevates the system performance to achieve dual intent of OPF
coupled with voltage stability and effectiveness is assessed by
random overloading of transmission lines to ascertain best TCSC
location and secured reactance limit. The bus data, line data and the
limits of control variables are estimated from [
17, 18]. The fuel cost
coefﬁcient of IEEE 14 bus system is referred from [ 19]. The
Newton–Raphson power ﬂow method is effectively employed to
calculate the power ﬂow solution before and after setting TCSC.
The test systems are evaluated using traditional GSA, fuzzy-GSA,
RBFNN-GSA and the proposed method wherein outcomes are
assessed and contrasted in each case.

5 Conclusion
The work presented in this paper emphasises on achieving secured
OPF but without compromising voltage stability even under heavy
loading condition and candidly displays four approaches of GSA,
fuzzy-GSA, RBFNN-GSA and IGSA-FA to achieve the same. The
proposed method of IGSA-FA generates superlative results with
optimised TCSC location providing minimum generation cost, TCSC
cost and diminished power losses for standard IEEE benchmark 6
and14 bus systems. The power ﬂow security is suitably analysed by
each method as line outage reduces the load power limits which are
restored eventually by optimally setting the installed TCSC to
rebuild secured power ﬂow of transmission lines and retain stable
voltage proﬁle. The result comparison for IEEE 30 bus system for
OPF with respect to cost functions reveals the superior performance
of the proposed algorithm for better optimal solution with enhanced
computational speed. The comparison among all the methods by
graphical representation, results and statistical analysis of Individual
relative error (%) manifest the escalated performance of the proposed
method.
